review_scope: read-only interpretation of fixed-cut target, completed dynamic and fixed-B pointwise comparisons, and prior-block collapse hypothesis; no model execution

core_target.per_parent: q_i(psi) = K_i(psi) / Z_i, where K_i = prior_D(psi|U_i) * joint_likelihood and Z_i = integral K_i dpsi, 0 < Z_i < infinity
core_target.outer_mixture: p_cut(U_i,psi) = w_i q_i(psi), preserving original upstream w_i (M01 masses are 1/8)
core_target.forbidden_for_this_target: normalizing w_i*Z_i across parents; that changes the protected cut into an evidence-updated joint posterior

evidence_assessment.dynamic: V3 completed prescribed 27 pointwise calls (8 parents x 3 points plus parent0 revisit); this supports call/pointwise numerical reuse at those states only.
evidence_assessment.fixed_B: independent native parent index 1 anchor passed at 3 common states, including all factor entries, rates and physicals within declared tolerance; maximum logp error 1.7578713595867157e-8 and factor error 1.30385160446167e-8. Two scalar finite-difference comparisons are not analytic or full 662-coordinate gradient verification.
evidence_assessment.missing: Native fixed baselines for parent indices 2–7 remain absent. No Z_i, normalized conditional bank, inference diagnostics, or prediction qualification is established. Fixed outer masses remain 0.125.
evidence_assessment.normalization: Pointwise equality at finite states and gradient checks do not establish 0<Z_i<infinity, numerical integration accuracy, conditional convergence, or adequate support/tail exploration. A proper per-parent conditional bank plus diagnostics is needed before mixing predictions.

counterexample.construction: Eight equal-mass parents; each conditional kernel is constant over two states, with seven kernels (1,1) and one (2,2). Thus all conditional laws are exactly (1/2,1/2), but Z=(2,...,2,4).
counterexample.cut: retains parent masses 1/8; an observable unique to the last parent has probability 1/8
counterexample.evidence_reweighting: would assign 1/9 to each of seven parents and 2/9 to the last; that observable becomes 2/9
counterexample.implication: within-parent evidence/normalization must not update protected outer masses under population_cut_v1

feasible_next_tests: Complete the independently source-pinned fixed-state native baselines for parents 2–7 if the approved exhaustive source-equivalence proof is not accepted; compare identical full points, all factor ownership and physical outputs, with masses kept outside each logp.

For each parent separately, build a genuinely normalized conditional bank or validated integration/importance estimate; check support, finite normalizer, ESS/error and full conditional MCMC diagnostics. Normalize weights only within parent, then combine parent-specific rows using original 1/8 masses.

If using a collapsed frailty representation, compare reduced density and theta-gradient pullback against original logp after accounting exactly for the normalized transformed nuisance-prior block and Jacobian; raw full-coordinate pointwise logp equality is not the claim.

On reconstructed complete rows, verify one shared kappa per row and all event frailties conditionally generated from it, then compare joint prediction law against the unchanged prediction kernel. Preserve parent/row/RNG lineage; test active-count and additive-poll-floor counterexamples before claiming observed-likelihood factorization.

frailty_collapse.status: source-algebra hypothesis/design only; not implemented or compiled-verified
frailty_collapse.condition: If every observed likelihood factor is independent of kappa and all 54 G_e after exact source-level cancellation, integrating normalized LogNormal(kappa) and conditional Gamma(G_e|kappa) priors leaves the theta marginal unchanged.
frailty_collapse.not_pointwise: Removing kappa/G changes dimension and removes their prior density/Jacobian. Equality is only a marginal-law claim; compare theta gradients in shared coordinates with the correct transformed prior accounting.
frailty_collapse.joint_prediction: For each retained complete row, draw one kappa and then all 54 event G values conditionally on that same kappa in pinned event order; recompute event and category intensities and use the existing shared-event participant/prediction path. Independent per-event kappa, G=1, or reused frailties changes joint predictions.
frailty_collapse.counterexamples: An observed absolute-count/report factor involving G, additive poll epsilon preventing common-G cancellation, or any hidden nuisance-dependent observed factor defeats prior-only collapse. The exact toy supports its invented discrete-kappa math only, not the actual continuous-kappa compiled model.

distinction_from_owner_experiment: The owner's event-shape coordinate experiment retains latent event-shape variables and changes coordinates; this review's frailty-collapse route would remove a prior-only block from the observed likelihood and reconstruct it for prediction. They are distinct alternatives. No claim is made that either remedies sampling diagnostics or improves predictive skill.
